name: Apixaban
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: For atrial fibrillation, the US apixaban label lowers the dose to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of three criteria apply: age 80 or older, weight 60 kg or less, serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or more. In hemodialysis the label supports the usual dose (2.5 mg if age ≥80 or weight ≤60 kg); small pharmacokinetic studies disagree on whether 5 mg twice daily is excessive, and outcome trials were underpowered (specialist decision).
kidney_function_basis: Atrial fibrillation dosing uses serum creatinine (≥1.5 mg/dL), age and weight, not eGFR or CrCl bands.

bands.recommendation: Atrial fibrillation (AF): 5 mg twice daily; 2.5 mg twice daily if 2 of: age ≥80 years, weight ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL. Venous thromboembolism (VTE) treatment, prophylaxis: no kidney adjustment (label).
bands.short: AF 5 mg BID; 2.5 mg if 2 of 3 criteria

bands.recommendation: As above; serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL counts as one criterion (label). Do not reduce the dose for kidney function alone; 2.5 mg twice daily requires 2 of the 3 criteria.
As above (label gives no separate band).
bands.short: As above; no separate label band

bands.recommendation: As above. Not separately addressed in the label. Specialist input.

hd.text: Label: trials did not enroll dialysis patients; the usual recommended dose (5 mg twice daily, or 2.5 mg twice daily if age ≥80 or weight ≤60 kg) gives exposure similar to ARISTOTLE; VTE indications need no adjustment. Literature: 2.5 mg twice daily gave exposure comparable to 5 mg in normal kidney function and 5 mg twice daily was supratherapeutic (Mavrakanas 2017). Small trials (RENAL-AF, AXADIA-AFNET 8) were underpowered for outcomes. Specialist decision.

pd.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.

crrt.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.

dialyzable: Minimally: dialysis clearance about 18 mL/min; exposure about 14% lower on dialysis; 92–94% protein bound (label). Mavrakanas 2017: about 4% removed in a session.

pediatric.approved_ages: Treatment of VTE and reduction in risk of recurrent VTE: birth and older, after at least 5 days of initial anticoagulation; not studied under 2.6 kg (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Weight-tiered fixed doses (label Table 1). Example tiers: 2.6 to <4 kg, 0.3 mg twice daily for 7 days then 0.15 mg twice daily; ≥35 kg, 10 mg twice daily for 7 days then 5 mg twice daily. No mg/kg dose in the label.
pediatric.max_dose: 10 mg twice daily (days 1–7), then 5 mg twice daily (≥35 kg tier).

renal.recommendation: 2 years and older: not recommended if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2 (label, bedside Schwartz).

pediatric.neonates: Under 2 years: not recommended with inadequate kidney function defined by sex and postnatal age (label Table 12). Not studied under 2.6 kg.
pediatric.notes: The label's pediatric VTE trial estimated GFR with the bedside Schwartz equation (0.413 x height/serum creatinine), matching this site's pediatric bands.
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: KEY CONFLICT: label supports the usual dose (5 mg BID) in hemodialysis; Mavrakanas 2017 (n=7) found 5 mg BID supratherapeutic and 2.5 mg BID adequate. RENAL-AF used 5 mg BID (2.5 mg if ≥80 y or ≤60 kg); AXADIA used 2.5 mg BID. Dr. Rivero to choose the site's position.
Label is silent on eGFR <15 not on dialysis and on PD.
pediatric: Pediatric dosing is weight-tiered fixed mg, not mg/kg. The <2-year kidney-function table (Table 12) is not reproduced; link to label.
